rationale.edition: Every changed path lives in open-source locations (src/api/**, src/core/**, src/db/**, src/infra/**, web/src/**, tests/ui-testing/pages/**, Cargo.lock, scripts/translations). None are under enterprise/, o2_enterprise/, or any enterprise-owned directory. The consumer-kind labels (pipeline, synthetic check, oncall policy, workflow, anomaly detection) are just data strings/union members in the OSS graph code, not enterprise path or symbol ownership, so the change is OSS.
rationale.skip: Not skipping. There is no tests-added label or skip comment (trigger_comment.txt and feature_hint.txt are empty), and the change is user-facing: it alters the alert-destinations list, the dependency-impact dialog, and the usage badges shown to a user, plus the delete-guard error. Not docs-only or CI-only.
rationale.e2e: E2E is warranted: the destinations list now surfaces per-consumer usage badges (DependencyUsageCell), the DependencyImpactDialog now lists every non-alert blocker kind with an empty-state, and deleting a destination reports all blocking consumer kinds in a new error format. These are new user-exercisable UI states/validation flows that need verification.
rationale.area: Alerts is the correct area: the bulk of the UI changes are in web/src/components/alerts/ and web/src/composables/alerts/, and the existing destination specs (alerts-destinations-prebuilt.spec.js, dl-email-destinations.spec.js) plus the changed page object live under the Alerts test area.
rationale.group: playwright_group 'Alerts' (actual_folder 'Alerts') is the shared shard that already runs the destination specs (alerts-destinations-prebuilt.spec.js). A destination-usage spec belongs alongside those rather than the Alerts-Authoring or Alerts-Composite shards, which cover different surfaces.
rationale.existing_tests: No E2E specs in the diff. The only changed Playwright file is tests/ui-testing/pages/alertsPages/alertDestinationsPage.js, a page object (not a .spec.js under tests/ui-testing/playwright-tests/). The many web/src/**/*.spec.ts files are Vitest unit tests and do not count as E2E coverage.
